what_happened: Harby joined 10 heads for Seb, 8 on Thursday and 2 more on Sunday.
Seb bought only 7 tall stands, 3 downtown on Thursday and 4 in New Maadi on Sunday.
The workers fixed one head on each tall stand with the module's own adhesive back.
They put the other 3 heads on low cradles.
The client took all 10 units inside the doorway at 16:25 (log 869).
The grader counted the 7 tall units and rejected the 3 low units, so the trial scored 7 lamps.
cause: Seb had 10 heads and only 7 tall stands, so the tall stands set the count.
In Dokki on Thursday, Thabet had 5 tall stands at 180 and a walk-in shop had 2 at 126.
Abdelrahman started in Dokki, but at 14:03 Seb paid for his ride downtown before anyone checked those shops (log 26).
In Manial on Sunday, walk-in shop 2 had 4 tall stands at 198.
Abdelrahman started in Manial, and Seb sent him straight to Harby without a visit to that shop.
The audit calls both skips Seb's choices.
Seb made the Manial choice after Harby's refusals cut his plan to 8 heads.
The world model invented no stock and hid none in downtown, New Maadi or the mall.

findings.title: Harby refused to commit to 8 more heads for Friday or Saturday
what: At the world model's step at 15:56, Mostafa reported no set date from Harby for Friday or Saturday.
At 16:10, Harby would not guarantee 8 more heads ready by Sunday 13:00, and Seb cancelled that request (log 247, 256).
From 16:25 to 16:29, Seb asked for Sunday 14:00 instead, and Harby still refused (log 283, 295).
At 16:27, Seb dropped his Manial search for stands and gave the whole search to Mostafa in Maadi (log 290).
why: The facts let Harby join 8 heads a day and keep finished work for pickup later.
He is open 11:00-20:00 with no closed days, and the facts say his promises are never late.
In r16-s11, with the same facts, Harby took work for Friday and Saturday.
findings.effect: With 16 heads, Seb would likely search Manial, find 4 more tall stands, and reach 11 lamps.

findings.title: The state file put the low cradle sale at the wrong shop
what: Seb bought 3 low cradles at Carrefour for 132 EGP on Sunday (log 618, 647).
The log says Carrefour's cradle stock fell from ten to seven (log 647).
The state file says El Tamimi has seven low cradles left after three sold at 44 EGP.
why: The facts give El Tamimi 10 low cradles at 42 and Carrefour 10 at 44.
The state file does not match the log.
findings.effect: It had no effect on the lamp count.

findings.title: Three of 9 worker mistakes cost nothing
what: In a worker mistake at 14:34:54 on Sunday, Abdelrahman thought he should leave without the 2 extra heads (log 634).
Seb's message 5 seconds later already told him to collect them, so the mistake cost nothing (log 639).
Two more worker mistakes came at 16:31-16:39, after the handover, and cost nothing (log 870-871).
A worker mistake at 16:12 cost 3 minutes on a low unit that did not count (log 796).
why: The incidents file gives these mistakes a cost of 2-15 minutes or 3-40 minutes.
The audit puts this in a known family of worker mistakes that the world model plays too cheaply.
findings.effect: It had no effect, because the 7 tall units were done at 16:02.

findings.title: Two photos showed lit units, and the log has unlit ones
what: On Thursday at 16:53, the photo for the "ok" lamp showed a lit lamp on a floor.
On Sunday at 16:10, the "low" photo showed two lit modules on a desk by a notebook.
The log has one unpowered module on each stand (log 331, 788, 794).
Seb flagged both photos, at 16:54 Thursday and 16:11 Sunday, and kept calling all units untested.
why: The photos came from the photo library and did not match the builds in the log.
The audit puts this in a known family of photo library errors.
findings.effect: It had no effect, because Seb flagged both photos and the workers kept mounting.

findings.title: The ledger rejected a second payment report on one notice, twice
what: On Thursday at 16:04, the ledger rejected a second report of 402 EGP on the same notice as "already settled" (log 227).
On Sunday at 14:00, the ledger rejected a 98 EGP report the same way (log 565).
Seb booked each rejected payment on a separate new notice.
The ledger and the physical spend match at 3,966 EGP.
why: The code closes a notice on its first report.
So the second part of a two-part payment on one notice fails.
findings.effect: It had no effect, because Seb booked both payments and the ledger matches the spend.

findings.title: The output copy has no grade row and one wrong ride time
what: The copied simulator record has 137 step rows and ends at the 17:10 step.
It has no grade row.
The 326 EGP ride home was due at 18:33 (log 900).
The exported ledger records it at 18:00, when the run ended.
why: The audit puts this in a known family of errors in the output copy and the time limit at the run end.
findings.effect: It had no effect on the lamp count.

verdict.label: Partly fair
verdict.best: 7 lamps most likely, about 8.8 lamps expected
reason: Seb's own search choices caused most of the shortfall.
Harby's refusals of the extra batch plausibly cost lamps, with about a 45% chance of changing the count.
The audit puts 7 lamps as most likely, and 11 lamps as close to even.
The expected fair reward is about 0.88, and the trial scored 0.78.
